content:
Hello everyone,

I am looking at the theorem Int.abs_sub_lt_one_of_floor_eq_floor, which requires R to be a commutative ring. But it can be proved without assuming commutativity of R. I opened a PR which is currently running:
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36805

I wonder if this is good enough to merge or is it too small... Thank you!
It is surely not too small, thanks! It seems to me you are also removing IsStrictOrderedRing R.

I have added another PR, which adds the instances NeZero 1 and Nontrivial on floor semirings and floor rings. I'm planning to use these instances to reduce the assumption IsStrictOrderedRing to IsOrderedRing for several theorems about floor rings. I'll appreciate any feedback, thank you!

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36828
I left a comment there; that one looks more problematic to me

I've dropped a bit more PRs and now I get more questions in my head. If I'm going to continue weakening assumptions on floor rings, most likely I would duplicate Nat.cast_nonneg, Nat.cast_pos, Nat.cast_le, and Nat.cast_lt; this works in floor rings without IsOrderedRing assumptions (I've put this in a PR a few hours ago), but other than floor rings we would need IsOrderedRing.

A natural solution to me is to make another API that encapsulates the idea that Nat.cast (and maybe Int.cast too) is (strictly) monotone. Maybe this is in similar style to ExistsAddOfLE?
